_comment: Hymns, spirituals and national anthems, own arrangements (L1 plan, Task 10). Specs and references: tools/arrangements/hymns.py. Retrieved sources: content/_raw/references/ (gitignored). simple-gifts and swing-low-sweet-chariot are replaced by the plan's two spares for this task, austrian-hymn and a-mighty-fortress (see rejected).

pieces.title: When the Saints Go Marching In
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: a beginner's march tempo; the reference's score is in 2/4 at quarter = 120, which in the doubled note values used here would be quarter = 240
pieces.levelNote: Level 1: right hand in C position (C4 to G4) throughout, left hand single notes and open fifths C3 to G3; heuristic proposes 1 (score 1.23)
pieces.notes: The traditional tune, not the similarly titled 1896 hymn 'When the Saints Are Marching In' (Katharine Purvis and James M. Black). Written in 4/4 with the reference's 2/4 values doubled, so the beginner reads quarter and half notes. Left hand on C and G, with F under the IV chord.

reference.description: ABC score in the German article (section Melodie), C major, 2/4; the English article has no notation

pieces.title: Michael, Row the Boat Ashore
pieces.year: printed 1867 (Slave Songs of the United States)
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: comfortable beginner tempo (the reference score has no tempo mark)
pieces.levelNote: Level 1: right hand in C position with the A as a small stretch (C4 to A4, as in Twinkle), left hand single notes and open fifths C3 to G3; heuristic proposes 1 (score 1.13)
pieces.notes: The spiritual first printed in Slave Songs of the United States (1867), in the familiar version of the Wikipedia score, one verse. Right hand C4 to A4; left hand plays I, IV and V roots in whole and half notes.

reference.description: Score in the article, C major, 4/4

pieces.title: Old Hundredth
pieces.tempoSource: reference: the Wikipedia score plays at half note = 52, that is quarter = 104
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: the melody spans D4 to D5 and moves position, left hand root-position and inverted triads within a ninth in G major; heuristic proposes 3 (score 6.76; it overrates held left-hand triads, as for Amazing Grace)
pieces.notes: The psalm tune of the Genevan Psalter in its original rhythm (long first and last notes in each line), sung in English to 'All people that on earth do dwell' and the Doxology. Barred in 4/4; the left hand gives one triad per half bar.

reference.description: First score in the article: Genevan Psalter rhythm, G major

pieces.title: Holy, Holy, Holy (tune Nicaea)
pieces.tempoSource: reference: the Wikipedia score's \midi block plays half note = 90 in 4/2; with the values halved here that is quarter = 90
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: melody D4 to D5 in D major (two sharps), left hand triads within a ninth following the New English Hymnal's harmony; heuristic proposes 3 (score 7.20; it overrates held left-hand triads, as for Amazing Grace)
pieces.notes: Dykes's tune for Reginald Heber's hymn, after the New English Hymnal setting, with the 4/2 values halved into 4/4. The left hand simplifies the hymnal's lower three voices to one triad per half bar.

reference.description: Score in the article (The New English Hymnal setting), soprano, D major

pieces.title: A Mighty Fortress Is Our God (Ein feste Burg)
pieces.catalogue: chorale melody, as set by J. S. Bach in BWV 80
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: a broad chorale tempo, quarter = 80
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: melody D4 to D5 in D major (two sharps), left hand triads within a ninth; heuristic proposes 3 (score 7.37; it overrates held left-hand triads, as for Amazing Grace)
pieces.notes: Spare for this task, replacing Swing Low, Sweet Chariot (no reliable notated source). Luther's chorale in the even rhythm of Bach's closing chorale of the cantata BWV 80, with the repeat of the first two lines written out and the fermatas left out.

reference.description: Score of the closing chorale in the article on BWV 80: the soprano, D major

pieces.title: La Marseillaise
pieces.catalogue: Chant de guerre pour l'Armée du Rhin
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: a steady march for level 2; the 1792 source's \midi block plays quarter = 120 ('Temps de marche animée')
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: melody G4 to A5 with dotted rhythms and the minor-key colour of the middle section, left hand triads and bass notes in C major; heuristic proposes 3 (score 6.48; it overrates held left-hand triads, as for Amazing Grace)
pieces.notes: The melody of the first edition (Bignon, 1792) as typeset for Mutopia, with the sixteenth-note pickups straightened to eighths and the closing ritornello left out. Left hand: half-bar triads and single bass notes.

reference.description: Mutopia 1891, first edition (Bignon 1792), public domain: the voice part, C major

pieces.title: God Save the King
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: a stately anthem tempo, quarter = 84
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: melody E4 to D5 in F major, left hand triads within a ninth, mostly one per bar; heuristic proposes 3 (score 6.30; it overrates held left-hand triads, as for Amazing Grace)
pieces.notes: The British national anthem (the same tune as 'My Country, 'Tis of Thee'), in F major. Left hand one triad per bar, two or three in the cadences.

reference.description: Tune AMERICA on hymnary.org: the soprano of The Cyber Hymnal's score #49 linked there, F major

pieces.title: Austrian Hymn (Gott erhalte Franz den Kaiser)
pieces.tempoSource: reference: the Wikipedia score's \midi block plays quarter = 90
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: melody D4 to G5 in G major, several position changes, left hand triads within a ninth; heuristic proposes 3 (score 7.53; it overrates held left-hand triads, as for Amazing Grace)
pieces.notes: Spare for this task, replacing Simple Gifts (no readable notated source). Haydn's hymn for Emperor Francis II, first performed on 12 February 1797; the tune of the hymn 'Austria' and of 'Das Lied der Deutschen'. Both repeats written out.

reference.description: Score in the article, G major

rejected.reason: No notated text source could be read: the English, German and French Wikipedia articles have no score (only an image of the 1848 manuscript transcription on Commons); the hymnary.org melody score is behind a publisher's licence gate and its Cyber Hymnal entry is the copyrighted 'Lord of the Dance'; cpdl.org refused the request. Replaced by the spare austrian-hymn.

Sources disagree: the Wikipedia articles (en, de, fr, it) have no score; the only text score, The Cyber Hymnal's MusicXML on hymnary.org, read twice gave measures that do not fill the metre and an opening that differs from the page's own incipit. Replaced by the spare a-mighty-fortress.
